[AMD][gfx1250] Ignore unit dims when checking the shared order for TDM ops (#12331)

When getting the order from the shared LL it will place unit dims at the
back, since they do not affect the physical layout, so we should ignore
them in the verifier.

commits.message:
[GLUON] Reject async copies between mismatched element types (#12341)

Fixes #12243.

Gluon's `async_copy.async_load` only checked that smem and pointer
shapes match. An fp32 pointer into an fp16 shared buffer compiled and
copied raw bytes (wrong values), and the reverse faulted with a
misaligned address at runtime. `smem.store` has always rejected the same
mismatch at compile time; the async path now does too.

Changes:

- Frontend checks in all three Gluon async-copy builtins: NVIDIA
`ampere.async_load` (Hopper and Blackwell share it through re-export)
and AMD `cdna4.global_load_to_shared` / `cdna5.global_to_shared` +
`shared_to_global` (both copy directions). The pointer's element type
must equal the destination dtype, mirroring `smem.store`'s contract.
- An IR verifier on `AsyncCopyGlobalToLocalOp` so producers that bypass
the Gluon builtins fail verification instead of lowering a mis-sized
copy.
- A frontend regression pins both mismatch directions (fp32→fp16 and
fp16→fp32) raising `CompilationError` at parse time.

Tests: the new case is red without the frontend check and green with it;
the full `test_frontend.py` sweep shows the same 41 pre-existing
environment failures on the untouched tree (they need ptxas, absent on
this machine) and zero new failures from the diff (565 → 567 passing,
the delta being the new test). The C++ verifier follows the existing
`verify()` idiom in Ops.cpp but was not rebuilt locally (no LLVM build
here), so its compile is covered by CI. The runtime byte-level repro
from the issue needs a GPU, which this machine does not have; the
compile-time rejection is the behavioral contract being added.

commits.message:
[GSan] Add memory access profiler (#12338)

Choosing GSan's shadow granularity and `write_once` policy currently
requires manual inspection. Add a `gsan-profile` instrumentation mode
that records observed accesses and reports granularity and write-once
candidates for each tracked storage lifetime.

The profiler uses a dedicated allocator with compact metadata, while
sharing allocation and descriptor helpers with GSan. A direct PyTorch
CUDAAllocator is installed explicitly before CUDA initialization;
profiling is enabled only inside `AllocationProfile`. Storage retirement
summarizes and resets metadata in stream order, allowing allocator reuse
without retaining tracked tensors. Reports are available after context
exit.

Supports multiple CUDA devices, shared IPC/FABRIC mappings, and
collective Gloo/NCCL reports. Unmanaged memory and raw allocator clients
are ignored. Runtime constants are shared through native bindings, and
the device entry points match the current atomic instrumentation ABI,
including vectorized atomic element widths.

Includes an explicit test bootstrap and regression coverage for storage
reuse, streams, graph capture, TMA, atomic accesses, and distributed
profiling. Recommendations describe observed instrumented executions and
require validation in a separate GSan run.

## Validation

- Rebuilt on GB300 and ran `make`.
- Full profiler suite: **110 passed**, including single-node multi-GPU
and Gloo/NCCL distributed cases.
- Startup isolation: **6 passed**; new vectorized atomic coverage: **8
passed**.
- Compiler lit suite: **305 passed, 2 unsupported**.
- Existing GSan allocator/race and TMA-marker checks: **19 passed**.
- Python syntax, Ruff, shell syntax, and diff whitespace checks passed.

Multi-node FABRIC tests were not rerun after this rebase.

commits.message:
[Runtime] Serialize class-valued constexprs for preload (#12430)

JIT cache hooks currently fail with `TypeError: Object of type type is
not JSON serializable` when a constexpr argument is a class, even though
ordinary JIT compilation accepts it.

Record class objects by module and qualified name, then resolve those
references in the same constant encoder/decoder used for JITFunction
arguments. Like the existing JITFunction support, this handles
references supplied directly as constexpr arguments. Class instances
remain unsupported, and unresolved class references (including
function-local classes) fail explicitly.

[AMD] Use new AMD CodeGen build and update test (#12391)

Pin the AMD codegen library to build 6, which parses "name=value" LLVM
flags, so values given through llvm_cl_opts now reach AMDGPU codegen.

Test llvm_cl_opts with string values: misched=ilpmax and misched=ilpmin

commits.comment: triton_kernels NVFP4 ROUND_UP scale 改为向上取整。问题：原先 ROUND_UP 直接用 nearest-even 转 E4M3，可能把 1.03125 舍入为 1.0（低于要求的 scale）。修复在 _downcast_to_mxfp.py 与 mxfp.py 的 torch 参考实现中一致实现：先 clamp(max=448) 转 scale_dtype，若结果小于未舍入值则按 uint8 位加一（E4M3 正数编码单调），并以 0x7E 作为饱和边界防止 448 继续进位。测试覆盖精确值/次正规/饱和/全部有限非负 E4M3 区间（含 3 个内点）、axis 0 与 -1、BF16/FP32 输入、masked 量化 helper；matmul 测试在 NVFP4 下先 apply_precision 再转 FP32 以保留参考精度、避免中间 BF16 舍入选错 ceil scale。属 triton_kernels 数值库代码，与编译器后端无关。风险中低（数值语义修正，可能改变既有 NVFP4 下游结果的量化 scale）。
commits.message:
[triton_kernels] Ceiling-round E4M3 scales for ROUND_UP (#12401)

## Summary

NVFP4 `ROUND_UP` currently casts the block scale to E4M3 with
nearest-even rounding, which can round below the required scale. For
example, a scale of `1.03125` becomes `1.0` instead of `1.125`.

Make `ROUND_UP` choose the smallest representable E4M3 scale greater
than or equal to the unrounded scale, saturating at `448`. Apply the
same behavior to the Triton implementation and PyTorch reference. Add
regression coverage for exact values, subnormals, saturation, every
finite nonnegative E4M3 interval, both supported axes, BF16/FP32 inputs,
and the masked quantization helper.

The matmul tests also preserve FP32 reference results through NVFP4
output quantization. This avoids an intermediate BF16 rounding step that
can select a different ceiling-rounded block scale.

## Validation

- All 11 [CI
checks](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/39651028615)
passed on `a0648d037699cb5e93022a068d8bc828674bba94`, including GB200,
H100, A100, AMD, macOS, and pre-commit checks.
- The confirming GB200 run passed after preserving FP32 in the matmul
test reference; test tolerances are unchanged.
- `git diff --check` and local YAPF, mypy, and installed Ruff checks
passed.

## New contributor declaration

- [x] I am not making a trivial change, such as fixing a typo in a
comment.
- [x] I have written a PR description explaining why the change is
needed.
- [x] Pre-commit checks passed in CI.
- [x] I have added tests in `python/triton_kernels/tests/test_mxfp.py`.
- [x] I have not added any `lit` tests.

commits.comment: FPSan 下 16 位 copysign 的 NaN payload 保留。问题：LLVM 可能把整数符号位操作识别为 llvm.copysign.bf16/f16，NVPTX 经 neg.bf16 规范化 NaN，破坏 FPSan 用浮点值承载整数 payload 的语义。修复：python/src/llvm.cc 新增 lowerNVPTXFCopySign，在 enableFpSan 时与 lowerNVPTXFAbs 一同调用，对 half/bfloat 的 copysign intrinsic（含 FixedVector）用内联 PTX 汇编实现 mag ^ ((mag ^ sign) & 0x8000)，三输入便于 ptxas 融合为单条 LOP3；通过 InlineAsm 阻止 SelectionDAG 再次识别为 copysign。跳过 hasNoNaNs 的调用。测试覆盖 half/bfloat、lanes 1/4、fpsan 与空模式，断言 PTX 中不出现 abs/neg.f16/bf16 且 xor/and 指令条数与 lanes 一致。风险中等：直接修改 LLVM lowering 的 inline asm，需保证寄存器约束 'h' 与 16-bit 类型在各 PTX 版本下正确；属 NVIDIA FPSan 专属路径。
commits.message:
[NVIDIA] Preserve 16-bit copysign NaN payloads under FPSan (#12418)

FPSan BF16 payloads can be corrupted after LLVM recognizes integer
sign-bit manipulation as `llvm.copysign.bf16`, exposed by #12319. NVPTX
can lower that intrinsic through `neg.bf16`, which canonicalizes NaNs. A
distributed BF16 collective consequently produced -4 where its FPSan
result should have been 1.

For FPSan compilation, lower FP16/BF16 `copysign` to bit-preserving
integer PTX operations after LLVM optimization. Use `mag ^ ((mag ^ sign)
& sign_mask)`, following [LLVM
#230107](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/230107), so ptxas can
fuse the three-input operation into one LOP3. Cover scalar and
fixed-vector forms alongside the existing FP32 `fabs` regression.

Validation on GB300:
- Four-GPU collective reproducer passes with fresh caches; the
unmodified compiler fails under matching conditions.
- All 10 focused compile-only cases pass (eight new copysign cases and
two existing fabs cases).
- All five existing payload tests pass: abs, cast truncation/extension,
cast extension, downcast placement, and the FP32 signaling-NaN loop.

Matched SASS checks on SM90 and SM100 confirm one LOP3 per FP16/BF16
element, versus two for the previous mask/mask/or sequence, for both
scalar and four-element vectors.
